newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil law makes all citizens organ donors.
newsitem.headline: Brazil law makes all citizens organ donors.

text.p: A controversial law that makes all Brazilians potential organ donors was approved by Brazil's government on Tuesday, a presidential spokeswoman said.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso vetoed a few clauses in the bill, which has prompted a storm of controversy since being passed by the Senate last month.
But the changes did not change the essence of the new law that allows federal authorities to use the organs of the deceased for transplants without the person's prior consent.
"We have moved from respect for death to respect for life," Health Minister Carlos Cesar Albuquerque said as Cardoso signed the bill into law.
Brazilians who do not want their body parts to be used in transplants must declare so on their identity cards or driving licenses.
The new law has bitterly divided the Catholic Church and civil rights groups, as well as the medical profession.

"Automatic donation is an abuse of one of the fundamental human rights, that of the individual's autonomy," Valdir Mesquita, head of the Federal Council of Medicine, told Globo newspaper in an interview published on Tuesday.

The bill was presented to Congress as a way of tackling a desperate shortage of donor organs in Brazil. At first, the government hesitated about backing such a wide-ranging bill, but has since argued that similar laws exist in countries such as Spain and Belgium.

Sen. Lucio Alcantara, who drew up the bill, said 60 percent of the 25,000 Brazilians receiving dialysis treatment for kidney disease could be cured if kidneys were available for transplant operations.

The law stipulates that relatives of the deceased must be consulted before their organs are used. It also requires the government to carry out annual campaigns encouraging families to offer the organs of deceased relatives for transplant.
